title: Thinking
coreMove: Convert gathered information into a usable distinction before deciding.
sourcePressure: The book closes by turning learning inputs into judgment, decisions, and connection-making rather than raw accumulation.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating more information as the same thing as clearer judgment.
sourceAnchorNote: Frozen sidecar contains no chapter-local named figure, named study, named place, or dated anecdote. Use fictional protagonists and keep source alignment at the concept and title-pressure level.

hook: Do not open Thinking with a generic unlocked potential claim.
Do not start with a definition of thinking.
counterintuition: Do not use a not X but Y correction shell.
Do not claim the opposite of common sense in generic coaching language.
tryThisNow: Do not use set a timer and reflect.
Do not ask the reader to journal broadly without a visible action.
examples: No repeated desk, kitchen, classroom, commute, or generic meeting shells.
No six examples built around timestamp plus named protagonist plus decision.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: planner turning a stack of reports into a zoning recommendation
exampleSpecs.stakes: a neighborhood vote hinges on one tradeoff
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Julia draws the tradeoff on tracing paper before recommending, forcing facts into a visible distinction.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: transparent tracing paper over a zoning map

exampleSpecs.audience: social worker interpreting mixed notes into a safe plan
exampleSpecs.stakes: a patient may return if the plan misses the real constraint
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Pavel asks which fact changes the decision, then separates medical readiness from home support on the whiteboard.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two columns on a portable whiteboard

exampleSpecs.audience: founder drowning in survey results and competitor screenshots
exampleSpecs.stakes: a launch price must be set by Friday
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Beatrice lays three price cards on the table and removes every data point that does not change the choice.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three matte price cards under a desk lamp

exampleSpecs.audience: analyst connecting testimony patterns to likely doubts
exampleSpecs.stakes: wrong interpretation can steer the trial team badly
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Andrew traces each juror reaction to the exact testimony moment before calling it a pattern.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: colored sticky flags on a transcript page

exampleSpecs.audience: architect weighing old photos against safety codes
exampleSpecs.stakes: one attractive choice could violate code or erase character
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Tomasz asks what each source can and cannot prove, then marks the decision boundary on the facade plan.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a faded facade photo clipped to a code page

exampleSpecs.audience: doctoral student turning readings into an experiment choice
exampleSpecs.stakes: months of work depend on the hypothesis being clear
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You write the claim, the rival explanation, and the next test on one index card before opening another paper.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: one index card beside a stack of papers

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm, using a question to the reader, a research aside only if source-supported, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

skillTargets: Identify when convert gathered information into a usable distinction before deciding. is needed in a new scenario.
Choose the visible action that matches Thinking rather than a nearby generic lesson.
Explain why the weak alternative fails without using recall-only phrasing.

tryThisNowSpec: Before deciding, write the distinction that would make one option different from the other.
